title: Chemistry, Bachelor of Science - Materials Option
sourceText: Arts [ARTS] CHEM 105 [PSCI] Students who have taken CHEM 101 must take CHEM 105 and 106, or 102 and 106. Highly qualified students are encouraged to take CHEM 116 in place of CHEM 106. ENGLISH 101 [WRTG] MATH 171 [QUAN] BIOLOGY 102 [BSCI], 106 [BSCI], or 107 [BSCI] CHEM 106 Students who have taken CHEM 101 must take CHEM 105 and 106, or 102 and 106. Highly qualified students are encouraged to take CHEM 116 in place of CHEM 106. HISTORY 105 [ROOT] MATH 172 CHEM 345 Humanities [HUM] MATH 220 MATH 273 PHYSICS 201 PHYSICS 211 CHEM 220 CHEM 347 CHEM 348 PHYSICS 202 PHYSICS 212 Social Sciences [SSCI] Complete Writing Portfolio CHEM 222 CHEM 330 CHEM 332 CHEM 370 or MBIOS 303 CHEM 398 Diversity [DIVR] Foreign Language (if needed) CHEM 331 CHEM 334 [M] Computational Elective: CPT S 121 or course approved by advisor Equity and Justice [EQJS] MSE 201 Foreign Language, if necessary, or Elective CHEM 333 CHEM 401 CHEM 480 CHEM 499 COM 400 [COMM], ENGLISH 301 [WRTG], or 402 [WRTG] [M] MSE 302 CHEM 410 CHEM 485 [CAPS] [M] MSE 321 MSE 323 Electives CHEM 503 or any 300-400-level MSE course not used to satisfy major requirements. Exit Interview The requirements for all bachelor of science chemistry options are the same through the first semester of the junior year. Admission to the Major Requirements A student may be admitted as a chemistry major upon declaring their intent to the department. To maintain good standing in the major, students must complete CHEM 105 and 106 (or 116) and MATH 171, each with a grade of C or better, by the time they earn 30 credits. Students must also have a grade of C or better in all CHEM and MSE courses. Failure to do so may result in the student being released from the major.
